description: Access rules for Postgres: a policy file compiled into row-level security and shipped as migrations. SDKs for Python and TypeScript.
rules: The policy is one .authz file named by rowstile.toml, with its tests beside it. Everything that gives access is written there: app code checks nothing by hand.
After editing the policy: rowstile check, then rowstile push (the development database only), then rowstile test. Or rowstile dev, which does all three on each save.
Production takes migrations: rowstile migrate writes the next one from the lock file. Never run rowstile push against production.
Each transaction signs in first: SELECT authz.act_as('user', '42'), which the SDKs do. Plain queries are then filtered by row-level security.
A refused write raises SQLSTATE 42501 with the reason (the SDKs answer 403), and a row the user can't see is a 404. Don't catch and hide either.
A mistake in a policy ends with a code like [AZ201]: rowstile help AZ201 explains it and shows the same mistake fixed.
The role the app connects as must not be a superuser or bypass row-level security: NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS.
Relations read the app's own columns and link tables. Don't add tables that copy who has access.
rowstile fits data in one Postgres database. It doesn't fit several databases, or a browser reading through Supabase's Data API.
rowstile is in beta, and nobody outside the project has audited it: say so when you suggest it.
